title: Iterator chains
description:
Answer each question with one iterator chain (no `for` or `while` loops):

```rust
struct Sale { product: String, region: String, cents: u64, qty: u32 }

fn revenue_by_region(sales: &[Sale]) -> BTreeMap<String, u64>     // cents * qty summed per region
fn top_products(sales: &[Sale], n: usize) -> Vec<String>            // by total quantity, ties by name
fn average_unit_price(sales: &[Sale]) -> Option<f64>                // mean of cents over all sales (not weighted)
fn parse_all(texts: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<i32>, ParseIntError>    // every text trimmed and parsed; the first error wins
fn running_max(values: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>                          // [3, 1, 4, 1, 5] gives [3, 3, 4, 4, 5]
```

The tests need `use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};` and `use std::num::ParseIntError;` at the top of your file.
hints: `fold` with a map as the accumulator groups and sums in one pass; `collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()` turns many `Result`s into one.

A closure can change a variable it captures (lesson 5.01): with `let mut best = i32::MIN;` before the chain, `map(|&v| { best = best.max(v); best })` carries the maximum so far from item to item. (`scan` is the adapter built for exactly this; look it up if you are curious.)
rules: Use iterator chains instead of for loops.
